note: The numbered streets and avenues (and Avenues A-D) are the grid of the Commissioners' Plan, adopted 1811-03-22: none was opened before it (most were opened decades later, block by block, as the building rule dates them).

Seventh Avenue was extended southward, as Seventh Avenue South, to link up with Varick Street in 1914, cutting through the older blocks of Greenwich Village (buildings in its path were demolished); Varick Street was widened at the same time (1917).
Sixth Avenue was widened and extended from Minetta Lane to Canal Street from 1926 (with the Holland Tunnel); the extension opened to traffic in 1930.
Kenmare Street was created in 1911 (the extension of Delancey Street toward Lafayette Street, cut through the blocks).
Lafayette Place: cut through the Vauxhall Gardens site by John Jacob Astor in 1825, from Astor Place to Great Jones Street.
Bloomingdale Road, opened in 1703 from about 23rd Street north: Broadway follows it (widened and paved as the Boulevard above 59th Street from 1868; the name Broadway since 1899).

The Boulevard: in 1868 the Bloomingdale Road between 59th and 155th Streets was laid out anew as a wide avenue; above 86th Street it left the old road's line (drawn from OpenHistoricalMap's trace until then, routes.csv).
The oldest thoroughfare of Manhattan: a Lenape footpath, then the Dutch road to the bouweries; colonists settled along it at Chatham Square in 1654 (the year used: the road is older).
Riverside Avenue (Drive) opened in 1880 from 72nd Street to the site of Grant's Tomb.
Manhattan Valley Viaduct (125th - 135th Street), completed mid-1902.

Extension north of the viaduct, begun December 1903; the section between 145th and 158th Streets formally opened February 1911 (the stretch from 135th Street is assumed to have opened by then: estimated).
Central Park's 66th Street transverse road was the first finished, opened December 1859.
Central Park's 79th Street transverse road (under Vista Rock) opened December 1860.
Central Park's 86th and 97th Street transverse roads opened in late 1862.
Central Park's 86th and 97th Street transverse roads opened in late 1862.
The first steel swing bridge was built in 1898 (replaced 1955-56 and 2004-05).
Opened in 1901 (replaced 2010).
A swing bridge was built here in 1884; today's bridge of 1910 doubled its capacity.
Opened to traffic 1905-08-24.
The first Cross Bay bridge opened in 1925 (replaced 1939-06-03 and 1970).
Built from 1894, opened to traffic November 1909 (161st Street to Mosholu Parkway; the stretch south of 161st Street, the former Mott Avenue, is left to the building rule).
The original Pelham Parkway was built in 1911 and opened in 1912 as a two-lane road (today's westbound lanes); today's parkway dates from 1935-37.
Opened 1963-02-06 as the Sheridan Expressway (a boulevard since 2019-12-11).

The new boulevard (Thomson Avenue and Hoffman Boulevard widened after the Queensboro Bridge) carried a trolley line from 1913; widened again in the 1920s-30s with the subway. One year for the whole boulevard: estimated (the roads it absorbed are older).
The parkway's northern half was completed in May 1874; the extension to Coney Island was finished 1876-11-11 and opened 1876-11-18 (the later date is used for the whole parkway).
Graded between Washington and Ralph Avenues by August 1871, almost completed by 1874.
The extension to Bushwick Avenue had been completed by 1897.

An Indian trail ('the ancient pathway' in a 1652 deed, the 'wagon path' in 1682), made the King's Highway in 1704. Today's boulevard was widened and straightened in the 1920s: where it left the old line the year is estimated (OpenHistoricalMap's trace of the old line is in routes.csv).

The first ride to lay out the post road between New York and Boston started 1673-01-01 (the road follows older trails: the year the post route was laid out is used; today's US 1 was widened and in places straightened: estimated where it left the old line).
Estimated: the company which built the Paterson and New York Plank Road received its charter 1851-03-14 (the charter date is used; the plank road across the meadows opened soon after).
